title: AO Tooling
description: One tool in the AO Commons tooling registry: software that autonomous organizations are built on or run with. Distinct from ao.schema.json — a tool is not an AO, however many agents it hosts. Schema version 0.1; expect breaking changes until 1.0.

id.description: Stable slug. Must match the filename and never change once published.

summary.description: What the tool does, in one or two neutral sentences. Descriptive, not promotional — vendor copy is a source, not a summary.

launched.description: First public availability, as YYYY, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD. This is public launch, which may be well after the repository was created.

categories.description: What the tool is for. Multiple values allowed.

agent_model.description: How agents participate in the tool: as managed workers, as identity-holding peers, as orchestrated teams. One or two sentences. This is the field that makes the tooling registry worth keeping — it records what shape of organization the tool actually makes possible.

human_controls.description: The oversight primitives the tool ships: budget caps, approval gates, pause and terminate, permission scopes, audit trails. Concrete mechanisms, not assurances. Where a tool provides none, say so — that is a finding, not a gap in the record.

maintainer.description: The organization or project behind the tool. Never an individual person — this registry describes software and the entities that ship it.

open_source.description: Tri-state rather than boolean, so an unresearched tool is never silently recorded as proprietary.

license.description: SPDX identifier where there is one (MIT, Apache-2.0, AGPL-3.0), or "proprietary".

model_agnostic.description: Whether the tool works across model providers or is tied to one.

protocols.description: Open protocols the tool speaks (e.g. nostr, mcp, a2a, activitypub).

used_by.description: Registry `id` slugs of autonomous organizations known to run on this tool. The cross-link that makes the two collections worth keeping in one repository.

sources.description: Evidence for the claims in this record. At least one required.
